claims.text: An approach incorporating configurational disorder and phase-diagram-inspired parameters can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Parameters derived from binary phase diagrams can be used to screen HEA compositions and predict their phase constitution.
Dynamic amorphization models can predict nanostructural behavior relevant to HEAs.
Amorphous or ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface structures reduce shear strength.
An ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer reduces wear in an HEA.
Amorphous or ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layers enhance phonon scattering.
The target materials are single-phase, disordered HEAs with high configurational entropy and a uniform solid-solution structure.
The predictive algorithm uses first-principles-informed models.
Compositions selected by the algorithm will develop dynamic-amorphization-related near-surface amorphous or nanocrystalline layers.
The approach is applicable under ambient temperature and pressure.
The approach applies only when the alloy does not decompose into intermetallic phases.
Selected HEAs will form an ultra-nanocrystalline or amorphous near-surface layer.
Selected HEAs will contain a high density of grain boundaries.
Disorder and grain boundaries dramatically shorten the phonon mean free path.
Shortening the phonon mean free path reduces phonon thermal conductivity relative to predictions from conventional ab initio or crystallographic models.
The proposed approach will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 15–20% relative to traditional methods.
Microstructural signatures such as amorphous near-surface layers will correlate with high phonon scattering.
Current thermal-conductivity prediction approaches rely solely on ab initio calculations or crystallographic descriptors and omit phase-diagram and disorder mechanisms.
The approach may fail when phase separation, intermetallic formation, or ordered microstructures dominate.
The magnitude of predictive improvement will vary with composition and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines the 15–20% improvement as an increase in predictive accuracy, whereas the falsification rule operationalizes it primarily as a 15–20% reduction in measured conductivity relative to conventional predictions or controls. Prediction error and material conductivity are different quantities.

The approach is framed as selecting alloys with low conductivity by predicting disorder-related structures, but the falsification rule treats failure to observe the targeted surface structure as sufficient for falsification even if the approach accurately predicts low conductivity. This makes structural mediation mandatory in the benchmark despite the main predictive claim being about conductivity.
